rootCauses.summary: NightView.build reconstructs core hunt geometry together with 100 procedural forest trees and 130 edge-clutter placements synchronously on the same click path that enters the hunt.
rootCauses.prediction: Moving non-interactive forest/edge decoration into bounded post-entry batches shortens the click-to-hunt main-thread block while converging to the same decoration counts.
rootCauses.falsifier: The first hunt still performs all decorative batches synchronously or the final staged world loses the deferred decoration.

rootCauses.summary: claimAndEnter calls newSession, and newSession calls view.build before mode becomes hunt and the title/HUD are swapped, so the browser cannot paint the hunt state until the expensive scene rebuild returns.
rootCauses.prediction: Core scene/session ownership becomes visible before deferred decoration drains, without changing input, combat, extraction or save semantics.
rootCauses.falsifier: The hunt mode/HUD still waits for all decoration work or gameplay starts against an incomplete interactive core.

observation.summary: Immutable Cloudflare staging for source afde80d shows a valid title, then the 狩夜へ click is followed by a 14.419s long task on hosted Chromium/SwiftShader. The first hunt snapshot eventually reaches mode=hunt, but sampled FPS is 2 while the transition settles. Source inspection shows the click synchronously runs NightView.build, including procedural forest and edge decoration, before the hunt UI swap completes.

conditions.scenario: cold open -> TAP -> title -> 狩夜へ -> first hunt

notVerified: full hunt completion in this baseline

evidence.statement: version.json.commit matches sourceSha; after #begin click a 14.419s long task occurs and hunt snapshot reports fps=2 while settling.
The click awaits character readiness, then newSession invokes view.build before mode/hud transition is completed.
A single synchronous build constructs interactive world plus 100 procedural forest trees and 130 edge-clutter placements before returning.

hypothesis.cause: The first-hunt entry path mixes interactive scene construction with non-interactive decorative generation in one synchronous task and performs that task before the hunt state can paint.
hypothesis.prediction: Stage the build: finish the interactive core synchronously, enter hunt, then drain decorative work in bounded animation-frame batches. This will reduce the dominant click-time long task without changing the eventual scene or gameplay systems.
hypothesis.falsifier: Same-condition After retains a comparable >10s click-time long task, never reaches a painted hunt before decoration completes, or final decoration counts differ.

candidates.reason: Preserves final visual density and gameplay geometry while moving only non-interactive decoration off the click critical path.
Moves the same stall into title time, increases simultaneous scene memory and does not remove the long synchronous task.
Would improve timing by visibly reducing scene richness instead of fixing scheduling.

implementation.summary: Split decorative forest/edge construction from the interactive core, run it in cancellable bounded frame batches for hunt entry, and keep title build/full scene compatibility.

limitations: Portable balance probe does not measure render scheduling; mark coverage outside.
Hosted Chromium timing is evidence for this staging environment, not a physical Pixel Fold benchmark.
